llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Android automation bridge that can read and control a connected phone, with meaningful privacy and confirmation guidance included.

dimensions.detail: The skill relies on adb, uiautomator2, Appium, OCR packages, localhost Appium access, screenshots, clipboard, and accessibility tree reads, all of which are proportionate to the advertised phone automation purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup is manual and transparent: a Python virtual environment, documented package installs, and optional Appium daemon startup; no hidden installer or automatic persistence was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The scope is broad because it can control any connected Android app, but the skill explicitly tells agents to use it only for user-requested phone-control tasks and to confirm irreversible actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent Appium daemon mode is opt-in, IPC and screenshot directories are created with 0700 permissions, IPC files are 0600, and screenshot retention is disclosed, though users should be aware screenshots persist locally until cleaned or overwritten.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Android app automation via OCR, accessibility data, Appium, taps, scrolling, and typing; the code implements those capabilities without unrelated exfiltration or destructive behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving an agent practical control over a connected Android phone. Use it for explicit tasks, review actions before orders or payments, do not provide PINs or payment secrets to scripts, and run the cleanup command or inspect the private cache if screenshots may contain sensitive information.
llm.findings:
[TT2] expected: The Appium launcher inherits Android SDK environment variables, which is a reasonable local tooling pattern for this purpose; it is worth hardening against hostile local environments but does not show hidden or unrelated behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: The Appium screenshot command saves a full phone screenshot locally, but screenshot capture is an advertised command and the skill discloses private storage for screen data.
[SQP-2] expected: The OCR workflow necessarily captures and processes screen images to locate text and coordinates; this is central to the skill's purpose and is disclosed, including that screenshots can contain personal data.
[SQP-2] expected: Clipboard-based text entry is disclosed as the workaround for Chinese input on locked-down devices; users should avoid using it for secrets even though payment credentials are explicitly left to the user.
